assessment: All 21 retained physical pages were text-read and visually inspected, including seven figures and all panels, four tables, captions, legends and six native equations. Thirty-six limited checks, nine steel rows, four compressor examples, three conditional fleet rows and eleven pure-state rows do not reproduce native author models. Exact original checks qualify the prior-conditioning attribution and offshore-heating assumptions. Preserve the 2800 kg/s annual-rate conflict, 877/887 km route discrepancy, diagram state differences and approximate costs. No accepted operating/GHG input changed; underlying originals, assets and native models remain open.

sections.assessment: Kwangu Kang, Youngkyun Seo, Daejun Chang, Seong-Gil Kang and Cheol Huh. Energies 2015, 8:2176–2196; DOI10.3390/en8032176. Received 16 December 2014, accepted 16 March 2015, published 19 March 2015. Three institutional affiliations; article CC BY 4.0. Article licence does not supply or license absent HYSYS cases or commercial databases.

Read both route lengths, 1/3 Mt/year cases, 33/28 and 21/23 USD/t cost comparisons and qualified hub conclusion. These are projected transport costs on unequal routes, not observed operating or lifecycle benefits.

65 large projects operating or planned 2013, 592.9 Mt Korean 2012 combustion emissions, ~50% power, 30% BAU 2020 target, 2017/2020/2030 deployment plans. Historical plans and CCS-as-intermediary framing do not verify current operation or unavoidable future requirements.

Coal and NG cost ranges from three reports, claim capture>50% of chain cost and weak country dependence. No matched capture utilities, energy suppliers, currency year or whole-chain comparison reconstructed.

sections.scope: Korean pilots, sources and storage context
sections.assessment: Read 10 MW amine/dry-sorbent pilots, >100 MW FID uncertainty, three plants, Ulleung 5 Gt resource and offshore-only rationale. No annual field pressure/well dataset or actual selected technology supplied.

sections.scope: Prior transport comparisons and conditioning attribution
sections.assessment: Read 200–1000 km crossover context and claim that cited recent work starts with>100 bar CO2. Exact Roussanaly 2014 original instead starts at 1 bar in both chains; do not apply that characterization to R013. Conditioning-inclusive comparisons already exist.

sections.scope: 2 Three transport scenarios and Table 1 diagrams
sections.assessment: All graphical arrows and annual capture lists read. S 1 one source 1/2/3/4/6 Mt/year; S 2 four combinations of 1/3 Mt at Boryeong/Hadong; S 3 two 1 Mt sources and three feeder modes to Ulsan, always offshore pipeline thereafter.

Coastal routing avoids mountains; Hadong lies on S 1 pipeline. Table 2 seven rows read. Ship/pipeline routes differ; S 2 table legs 617+270=887 km, prose later says 877. Ulsan selected as nearest harbor, not an independently optimized network.

Capture and storage excluded, compression/liquefaction included. Pumping to assumed wellhead state included, injection itself excluded. Read all subsystem arrows and pressure/temperature pairs; Injection label is a conditioning cost, not storage operation.

sections.scope: 3.1.1 Pipeline pressure, burial and diameter design
sections.assessment: 86–150 bar design band, 100 bar assumed wellhead because reservoir conditions undetermined, 1 m burial/28°C, booster assumptions. All candidate diameters/materials enumerated conceptually, not reconstructed from missing native schedules and hydraulics.

Nine material rows, eight with prices, plus X90 N/A. Eight NPS choices imply 64 priced candidates. Read rough 2015 internet-price provenance and Eq 1 constant-property friction/gravity variables; zero onshore elevation and minus 150 m offshore water-depth change are assumptions.

Read five-stage 2.36 ratio, 40/140°C temperatures, 40 MW train splitting, Eqs 2–4 and maintenance/electricity costs. Fixed train flow versus variable flow changes scale effects; native train powers/assignments absent.

Parker nonmaterial model transferred from natural-gas cost context; steel annulus weight and minimum-wall factors read. Greater available schedule thickness chosen, then cost comparison. No native full 64 design enumeration or cost validation reproduced.

Cargo 7 bar/-50°C, near-triple-point choice, closed propane/ethane cycle, pressure vessels and standards. Figure 4 feed 1 bar 25°C and product 6 bar/-53°C differ from main boundary; all refrigerant/CO2 components inspected. Case correspondence and full process balance unresolved.

sections.scope: Ship time, continuous injection and three ships
sections.assessment: 15 knots, 20 h loading/unloading, 2 h entry/exit, continuous direct injection and fixed three vessels read. Printed 2800 kg/s does not convert to 1 Mt/year. A 20 h direct-delivery interpretation gives an uncovered interval under stated voyage times; native schedule/control must be checked.

sections.scope: 3.2.2 Liquefaction costs and borrowed scale factors
sections.assessment: Read HYSYS economic estimation and delivered-equipment methodology, followed by 1.6 CAPEX/1.7 OPEX multipliers relative to compression. Financial multipliers do not give electrical duties, heat, cooling or full native liquefaction results.

sections.scope: Storage, carrier and injection conditioning costs
sections.assessment: Tank manufacturing 45% of total, ~280 USD/m³, 5% annual maintenance; hull/tanker/Clarksons analogies and 850 USD/ton fuel. Pump/heat to 100 bar 10°C includes no absolute native duties or verified heat source. Exact original heating regimes differ.

Ship tank and pressurization included; tank injection/discharge handling excluded. Pipeline 2 h buffer as parallel high-pressure pipes assumed. No continuous end-to-end service, actual buffer geometry, receiving chronology or weather performance established.

CRF 0.08 with 20 y/5% is rounding-compatible. All emitter/carrier/onshore/offshore/injection/hub and B/H/S labels read. Costs are per transported tonne; annualization assumptions do not create avoided/retained-mass accounting.

Read all component/total groups, 33/28 costs at 1 Mt and 21/23 at 3 Mt, 30–70% conditioning shares and 7 USD/t premium argument. Approximate bar heights are not exact native arrays. Literal twice-cost phrasing has an unresolved unit/total interpretation relative to plotted declines.

Both seven-bar panels compare four two-source designs with same-total single-source cases. Less upstream flow lowers some pipe costs but duplicated conditioning offsets savings; ship extra route raises costs. Preserve 877/887 discrepancy and distinguish section-versus-whole cost percentages.

Eleven bars, all categories and four marginal-addition choices read. Same-total single-source comparisons change geography; matched two-source averages have equal 1 Mt weights. Short 60 km shared trunk/two routes give small conditional savings, not universally uneconomic hubs.

Read comparative rankings, conditioning boundary, transport>20% of CCS cost proposition and future-capacity recommendation. Capture/storage omitted, no universal full-chain share proven; oversizing/technology superiority needs actual demand, uncertainty and boundary evidence.

sections.scope: Funding, contributions, conflicts, references and assets
sections.assessment: Funding from Korean Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries marine-storage technology project, all five author roles and no-conflict statement read. All 45 references and CC BY 4.0 inspected. No retained supplement/code/data availability statement identified. Original models and cited dependencies remain open.

visuals.inspection: Read three power-plant markers, Ulsan terminal and Ulleung basin marker. Geographic proximity is not an observed transport route, storage depth, pressure limit or availability record.

visuals.object: Table 1 all three scenario rows and transport diagrams
visuals.inspection: Inspected pipeline/ship arrows, two-source merge, Ulsan trunk and mixed Boryeong-ship/Samcheok-pipe option. Native text alone omits graphical labels; annual-volume lists and every arrow were checked in rendered layout.

visuals.object: Figure 2 panels(a)/(b), route legend and full caption
visuals.inspection: Red onshore, green offshore and blue dotted ship routes distinguish S 1/2 andS 3. Coastal paths and source/hub/sink markers read. Boryeong 530 km pipeline versus 724 km ship is not equal-distance comparison.

visuals.object: Table 2 seven distance rows and headers
visuals.inspection: All departure/destination/pipeline/ship cells read, including Hadong-Ulsan N/A.617+270=887 km differs from 877 prose; native values retained.60 km ship entry does not override S 3 fixed pipeline trunk.

Seven rows with merged transport labels read. Compression/ship liquefaction, carrier/tank/pump and hub pressurization boundaries retained. Capture/storage and hub tank handling exclusions are explicit in prose.

visuals.object: Figure 3(a) pipeline boundary and all state pairs
visuals.inspection: Dotted boundary and arrows inspected:1 bar 35°C→73.8 bar 40°C→150 bar 28°C→86 bar 28°C→100 bar 10°C. Capture/injection to storage outside; assumed wellhead condition does not certify native field service.

visuals.object: Figure 3(b) ship boundary and all state pairs
visuals.inspection: Read 1 bar 35°C feed, 7 bar/-50 Ccargo and 100 bar 10 Cdelivery, liquefaction, storage, carrier and injection-pumping blocks. No complete capture heat/power balance or actual operating timeline.

visuals.object: Table 4 nine steel grades, strength units and prices
visuals.inspection: All X42–X90 psi/MPa/price cells inspected. X90 priceN/A; eight priced grades match 64 cases with eight sizes. Internet price/currency/ton basis and standard edition need originals; no value silently corrected.

Enlarged all three propane stages, ethane compressor, two condensers, cooling-water inlet, four expansion valves/four separators, liquefier and recycle connections. CO2 path has two compressors, two coolers, three scrubbers. No unprinted heat duties or flows inferred.

Enlarged feed 1 bar 25°C and product 6 bar/-53°C, versus 35°C feed/7 bar/-50°C main scheme. Rounded 6 bar/-53 Ccan straddle saturation under a pure-fluid absolute-pressure illustration; no confirmed solid/hydrate or native HYSYS error claimed.

visuals.object: Figure 5 Scenario 1 component groups, legend and total
visuals.inspection: Four B 1/B 3 pipe/ship groups inspected. Red emitter bar is separate from stacked transport components and blue Sum. All six legend entries, axis USD/t CO2, caption and absence of error bars read. Native 33/28 and 21/23 are approximate prose labels, not exact digitized heights.

Seven labels B 1+H 1, B 2, B 1+H 3, B 3+H 1, B 4, B 3+H 3, B 6 and four emitter/pipeline colors read, including caption continuation. Native graph values remain approximate; no exact optimization replay.

visuals.object: Figure 6(b) ship panel and final caption
visuals.inspection: Same seven comparisons and four emitter/carrier/pumping categories read. Two-source geography and conditioning differ from concentrated single-source baseline; no common-mode universal efficiency factor.

visuals.object: Figure 7 all eleven bars and nine legend categories
visuals.inspection: Three B 1+S 1 hub modes; separate B 1/S 1 pipe/ship cases; B 2/S 2 pipe/ship cases inspected. Legend covers two emitters, two onshore routes, two carriers, hub, offshore, injection. Graph is cost-per-transported-tonne, not emissions or reliability.

visuals.object: All six displayed equations and variable prose
visuals.inspection: Every numerator, denominator, power, coefficient, index and unit read; Eq 2 enlarged. Native line regions preserved separately. There is no additional numbered objective, CRF or scheduling equation in retained paper.

equations.check: Eq 1 literal constant-property Darcy-style pressure/gravity relation. Native f, CO2 density, route profile and friction convention not supplied. Negative 150 mwater-depth term is not reservoir-depth pressure calibration.

Eq 2 literal m_train/N_train and pressure-ratio expression. Fixed train flow scales linearly with train count; fixed count has sublinear flow powers.40 MW threshold needs actual native power, not a guessed train allocation.
Eq 3 uses electric power in kW divided by 1000, capital USD. No native pump power or duty/efficiency inferred from coefficient.
Eq 4 uses kW and a booster-specific capital slope/intercept. Actual station count and operation remain unknown.
Eq 5 matches the exact annular-steel-volume identity with inner diameter D_i and outside D_i+2 t. Analyst geometry/density checks do not reconstruct native materials.

Eq 6 minimum-wall component uses native factors.8/.9/1/1; actual standard-thickness rounding and complete diameter/material selection unverified. Printed D_0 is distinguished from prose Do for outer diameter; no dimensional reinterpretation is inferred.
Analyst calendar conversion:1 Mt/y=31.70979 kg/s; continuous 2800 kg/s=88.3008 Mt/y. No repaired source unit or actual operating hours inserted.
Analyst conventional component gives.0802425872 for 5%/20 y, compatible with rounded.08. This is distinct from discount rate or full native cash flows.

Conditional direct-well delivery only during each 20 h unloading window, no buffer/weather/extra stop.724 km gives 96.12383 h cycle, three ships≤.6242 coverage. Different native injection durations/buffering may alter the bound; no recommended fleet inferred.
Equal 1 Mt source average in matched marginal comparisons is valid only with equal masses and common boundaries. Analyst 1/3 flows and 10/30 costs give 25 weighted versus 20 simple mean.

Conventional diagnostic interpretation of annualized transport cost, not another printed numbered equation. Not automatically cost per avoided/stored/retained tonne or a full author annualization replay.

variables.name: Transport/capture rate and annual denominator
variables.assumption: Scenario rates are assumed design loads; no measured capture fraction, pressure-limited annual injection or avoided-mass denominator.

variables.name: Route length and source location
variables.assumption: Unequal pipeline/ship paths, fixed coastal route, hub scenario changes geography.877 prose and 887 table sum unresolved; N/A does not mean zero.

variables.name: Pipeline min/max and wellhead pressures
variables.assumption: 86–150 bar band and 100 bar assumed wellhead; actual reservoir not determined. Flange/pump/network pressures are not geological maximum injection pressure.

variables.name: CO2 state temperature, phase and pressure basis
variables.assumption: Native gauge/absolute basis not explicitly stated. Pure-EOS comparisons assume absolute pressure and no impurities; diagram states differ and rounding can span phases. No hydrate/solid validation.

variables.name: Q_m, L, D_i, rho_CO2, f, g, deltaz
variables.assumption: Literal Eq 1 needs native density/friction/route. Onshore elevation 0 and offshore minus 150 mwater-depth are source assumptions, not calibrated reservoir datum.

variables.name: Grade, standard NPS and schedule
variables.assumption: Eight priced materials, eight sizes, 64 cases. Exact schedules/selection and metric-versus-short-ton pricing unverified. Higher strength alone does not establish minimum capital cost.

variables.name: m_train, N_train and compression ratios
variables.assumption: Parallelization above 40 MW needs native power. Five 2.36 ratios match rounded target; fixed train flow and fixed count are different scaling assumptions.

variables.name: W_p, Cpump, Cbooster
variables.assumption: Literal Eq 3/4 coefficients require kW-to-MW numerical conversion; no supplied actual station power or pumping duty.

variables.name: Ws, rho_steel, t, D_o, D_i
variables.assumption: Annular mass and minimum-wall relation checked with disclosed analyst geometry. Standard thickness rounding, corrosion/installation factors and native validation remain open. Eq6 prints D_0 while prose calls outer diameter Do.

variables.name: Pdesign, S, F, Lf, J, T
variables.assumption: Factors.8/.9/1/1 are design assumptions; mechanical/safety standard editions not independently validated. Tfactor is not CO2 temperature.

variables.name: Ship count, speed, port/loading/unloading and injection window
variables.assumption: Three vessels 15 knots 20 h load/unload 2 h entry/exit with continuous injection need full schedule.2800 kg/s correspondence unsupported; 20 h direct-delivery bound is conditional.

variables.name: Liquefaction CAPEX/OPEX ratios
variables.assumption: 1.6/1.7 relative to compression are not electric/heat ratios and do not give native process duties or suppliers.

variables.name: Tank cost and manufacturing share
variables.assumption: Approx 280 USD/m³; manufacturing 45% TOTAL, not 45% markup.5% annual O&M; actual volume/quote/native material basis unverified.

variables.name: Energy, fuel and maintenance prices
variables.assumption: Electricity.07, fuel 850, pipeline/compression 4% CAPEX, storage/carrier 5% CAPEX plus fuel. No source-specific GHG intensity or complete cost-vintage/inventory.

variables.name: Hub buffer and handling
variables.assumption: 2 hpipeline-buffer assumption, handling excluded. Ship-side inventories, timing, working capacity/quality and interruptions not verified.

variables.name: r, N, CRF and normalized cost
variables.assumption: 5%, 20 y, .08 rounded; not 8% discount. Exact cashflow timing, availability and currency bases remain unresolved.

variables.name: Emitter/cost-share, hub benefit and comparison weights
variables.assumption: Conditioning 30–70% is financial share, not emissions share. Changing source location/flow and equipment boundaries matters; some percentages concern subsegments.

variables.name: Resource, policy and future-capacity scope
variables.assumption: 5 Gt resource and 2017–2030 plans are not actual annual service. Future economies require demand/uncertainty evidence, not universal overbuilding or guaranteed climate benefit.

claims.claim: Pipeline/ship cost is approximately 33/28 USD/t at 1 Mt/y and 21/23 at 3 Mt/y.
claims.assessment: Source-specific transport ranking on 530/724 km routes; approximate labels, no universal threshold or climate factor.

claims.claim: 65 large CCS projects and Korean deployment targets motivate the study.
claims.assessment: Operating-or-planned 2013 inventory and 2017–2030 targets are historical, not current operating evidence.

claims.claim: Capture costs exceed half of CCS costs and vary little by country.
claims.assessment: Reported ranges need exact technology, utility, currency and system-boundary matching; no global invariance or full capture inventory established.

claims.claim: Korean 10 MW_pilots and technology selection lead to future full-scale capture.
claims.assessment: Pilots/FID plans do not establish selected process, annual availability or actual native utilities.

claims.claim: Ulleung has 5 Gt capacity and offshore is the appropriate storage option.
claims.assessment: Static source estimate and siting rationale require original geological evidence; no depth/pressure/well/injectivity dataset.

claims.claim: Recent transport work[11–14]starts above 100 bar and omits initial conditioning.
claims.assessment: Exact R013/B3-36 starts both chains at atmospheric 1 bar and includes conditioning. Qualification required; other editions and original claims remain open.

claims.claim: Three scenarios span one-source, two-source and hub transport.
claims.assessment: All diagrams/rates read. Candidate options are restricted scenarios, not proof of a global source-sink or infrastructure optimum.

claims.claim: Boryeong coastal pipeline avoids mountains and Hadong shares the same route.
claims.assessment: Fixed routing assumption with table distances; exact GIS, terrain, rights and route optimization unverified.

claims.claim: The cost boundary includes compression/liquefaction and transport-related pumping.
claims.assessment: Capture/storage excluded. Injection-pumping labels do not mean storage costs or observed physical injection are included.

claims.claim: 86–150 bar avoids abrupt compressibility and satisfies 900#flange constraints.
claims.assessment: Transport-design assumptions and cited standards need exact originals. Not reservoir pressure limits or proof of mixture/equipment safety.

claims.claim: 100 bar wellhead and 28 Cburied-pipeline temperatures support the design.
claims.assessment: Wellhead explicitly assumed because site conditions undetermined; summer-temperature datum and pure/mixed phase correspondence unverified.

claims.claim: Eight materials/eight sizes yield least-cost pipe design over 64 cases.
claims.assessment: Eight priced grades plusX 90 N/A consistent with 64. Native size/schedule/friction/property/cost choices and previous optimization not reproduced.

claims.claim: Eq 1 determines pressure difference and booster requirements.
claims.assessment: Dimensionally interpretable constant-property relation; actual f/rho/route and friction convention unresolved. Minus 150 mseabed elevation is not reservoir-depth evidence.

claims.claim: Five compressor stages with 2.36 ratio reach critical pressure.
claims.assessment: 2.36380 required ratio rounds to 2.36. Pressure alone does not guarantee liquid state; native compressor/pump correspondence at 73.8 bar 40 Cunverified.

claims.claim: Compression has no economies of scale because parallel trains are used.
claims.assessment: Conditional on fixed per-train flow and train scaling. Literal Eq 2 is sublinear in train flow at fixed count; 40 MW assignment and native powers missing.

claims.claim: Eqs 3/4 estimate pump and booster capital and 4% maintenance.
claims.assessment: Coefficients require kWnumerical scale; no native power or total station count. Literal examples are not equipment validation.

claims.claim: Parker costs are suitable for Korean CO2 pipeline transport.
claims.assessment: Natural-gas analogy and cited improved-model validation need exact original support and cost vintage; nonmaterial coefficients not fully supplied.

claims.claim: Steel weight and minimum-wall equations select optimum material/thickness.
claims.assessment: Annular identity checks; minimum-wall factors do not reproduce schedule rounding, corrosion/installation conditions or total 64 design optimization.

claims.claim: 7 bar/-50 Ccargo and closed propane/ethane liquefaction are economical.
claims.assessment: Case selection, not universal optimum. Native refrigerant flows, EoS, cycles, duties and availability assumptions absent; pure-fluid states do not validate full process.

claims.claim: Figure 4 represents the liquefaction scheme used for the transport case.
claims.assessment: Drawing gives 1 bar 25°C feed and 6 bar/-53°C product versus main 1 bar 35°C/7 bar/-50°C. Correspondence unresolved; rounded labels can span saturation, no guessed replacement states.

claims.claim: Cylindrical vessels meet ASME and IGC codes.
claims.assessment: Chosen design basis and cheaper/easier fabrication rationale need exact code/edition and native design; no present approval established.

claims.claim: 15 knot speed and 20 h load/unload, 2 h port times allow optimized three ships.
claims.assessment: Fixed fleet and native referenced schedule remain unverified. No weather, maintenance, concurrent operations or actual payload data supplied here.

claims.claim: Approximately 2800 kg/s corresponds to 1 Mt/year continuous injection.
claims.assessment: 365 day conversion gives 88.3008 Mt/year; 1 Mt/year is 31.70979 kg/s. Preserve literal rate; no corrected unit or batch schedule inferred.

claims.claim: Three ships provide continuous direct injection.
claims.assessment: If 20 h unloading is the direct-delivery window, 724 km roundtrip 96.12383 h allows≤62.42% coverage with three windows. Native control/buffer/longer injection could change interpretation; conditional bound is not full native infeasibility proof or a five-vessel design.

claims.claim: Pumping/heating to 100 bar 10°C avoids hydrate/freezing problems.
claims.assessment: Exact R035 supports need for heating but uses different 200–300 bar/15–20°C or platform 10–20°C routes. Neither pure EOS nor that original validates universal 100 bar 10°C or actual hydrate conditions.

claims.claim: HYSYS delivered-equipment evaluation supplies liquefaction costs.
claims.assessment: Underlying process/economic files, installation factors, cooling/heat/electricity and full output correspondence missing.

claims.claim: Liquefaction capital/OPEX are 1.6/1.7 times compression.
claims.assessment: Explicit financial proxy supported by cited comparison range, not heat/power ratios or complete native HYSYS results. Cannot infer energy from aggregate OPEX.

claims.claim: Storage costs about 280 USD/m³ with 45% manufacturing and 5% annual O&M.
claims.assessment: Manufacturing 45% of total implies 55% material; not 45% markup. Native volume, material quotes, vessel formula and currency basis still unverified.

claims.claim: An oil-tanker hull/fuel analogy and Clarkson prices estimate CO2 carrier cost.
claims.assessment: Payload/density, ship/cargo designs, year/ton basis and actual fuel-rate data need native evidence.850 USD/ton fuel is a price, not a GHG factor.

claims.claim: A hub needs tanks/pressurization and a 2 hpipeline buffer.
claims.assessment: Handling excluded; 2 h buffer in parallel pipes is a design assumption, not ship-side receiving capacity or demonstrated uninterrupted annual service.

claims.claim: CRF 0.08 with 20 y/5% normalizes transport costs.
claims.assessment: Conventional CRF.08024259 rounds to.08; not 8% discount. Actual annualization timing, currency/availability and full capital basis still missing.

claims.claim: Scenario 1 pipeline/carrier scale benefits lower transport unit costs.
claims.assessment: Reported pipe 33→21 andship 28→23 give 36.36/17.86% approximate savings. Conditioning/train scaling is conditional; plot costs not lifecycle emissions.

claims.claim: 3 Mt/y onshore/offshore costs are about twice 1 Mt/y costs.
claims.assessment: Literal wording has unclear per-tonne versus total-cost basis while plotted unit costs decline. No silent replacement with half, or a guessed total-cost interpretation.

claims.claim: Conditioning 30–70% share and 7 USD/tpremium can reverse mode choice.
claims.assessment: Financial boundary matters; conditioning-inclusive comparison already appears in R013. Approximate 7 USD/t cannot be converted into native power/heat without cost breakdown.

claims.claim: Additional Hadong flow reduces upstream pipe cost but duplicates conditioning.
claims.assessment: 280/530≈53% route fraction and approximate section/whole-cost percentages have different denominators. Equal-total cases retain different spatial source distributions.

claims.claim: Scenario 2 ship distance is 877 km, 22% longer than 724 km.
claims.assessment: Table legs 617+270=887 km→22.51%; prose 877→21.13%. Preserve both routes and 22% quote; rounding/exact basis unknown.

claims.claim: Two-source shipping costs more than the same-total single source.
claims.assessment: Duplicated conditioning and longer route are case drivers; carrier 7.5 versus 5 USD/t is a component comparison, not full-chain or GHG difference.

claims.claim: Hub pipeline around 28 USD/t is least costly among three Scenario 3 modes.
claims.assessment: Small plotted differences without full uncertainty/native arrays; conditional cost ranking, not universal hub technology or physical reliability conclusion.

claims.claim: Single-source B 2/S 2 cases are cheaper than two-source B 1+S 1 hub.
claims.assessment: Same total mass but different source geography and number of conditioners; not isolated causal effect of the hub.

claims.claim: A marginal additional B 1 route can use four hub/no-hub choices.
claims.assessment: Matched two 1 Mt source averages are valid at equal flows. Separate source costs must be mass-weighted for unequal flows; native schedule and existing-asset costs still need reconstruction.

claims.claim: Few sources and a short 60 km shared trunk make the hub uneconomic.
claims.assessment: Conditional to geography and compared cases. Paper also finds small shared-pipe savings versus matched separate routes and a handling-complexity tradeoff; not all hubs are uneconomic.

claims.claim: Transport can exceed 20% of total CCS costs and should be separated from storage.
claims.assessment: Cost-boundary recommendation is reasonable context; capture/storage excluded here, so universal full-chain share is not independently demonstrated.

claims.claim: Build higher-capacity systems to accommodate future transport.
claims.assessment: Recommendation based on scale effects; actual demand, time, discount, stranding, availability and resource limits require independent dynamic analysis.

claims.claim: Funding, author contributions and open access support transparency.
claims.assessment: Declarations read, not independent validation. CC BY 4.0 article does not provide or license absent commercial cost models/software.

claims.claim: The bibliography and prior author papers establish model support.
claims.assessment: 45 direct entries retained; only R013 andR035 have scoped original checks. Other originals and entire cited model chains remain unverified.

claims.claim: This case can supply pressure-constrained annual storage or complete capture utilities.
claims.assessment: Audit implication: it cannot close those requirements. Static 5 Gt, assumed 100 bar, the disputed 2800 kg/sandfinancial ratios are excluded as native operating/retention/GHG inputs.

claims.claim: Paper 1 should recognize existing conditioning-inclusive and source-specific transport comparison.
claims.assessment: Use as prior-art context with boundaries, route and schedule qualifications. No new accepted numerical inputs or source repairs; existing B2-12 HOLD preserved.

issues.finding: Printed 2800 kg/s is equated with 1 Mt/year continuous injection.
issues.action: Preserve native value; 365 day diagnostic gives 88.3008 Mt/year. No alternative unit or corrected design rate accepted.

issues.finding: Table 2 shipping legs sum 887 km while prose says 877 km and 22% extension.
issues.action: Keep table/prose separate; neither native route nor percentage silently repaired. Need exact GIS/basis.

issues.finding: Main scheme and liquefaction PFD state labels differ.
issues.action: Keep feed 35 versus 25°C andcargo 7 bar/-50°C versus 6 bar/-53°C. Pure absolute-pressure rounding illustration does not verify native process or identify a definitive phase error.

issues.finding: Static 5 Gt and assumed 100 bar wellhead do not provide native pressure-constrained annual service.
issues.action: Exclude rate/retention/field-calibration inference from these values. Need original geology, paired operating histories and well/pressure limits.

issues.finding: R013 is inaccurately grouped with studies starting above 100 bar.
issues.action: Exact original starts both chains at 1 bar with conditioning. Preserve qualified attribution; its excluded dehydration and different cases do not give full capture inventory.

issues.finding: R035 supports heating but not the assumed 100 bar 10°C or continuous fleet.
issues.action: Retain source-specific alternatives 200–300 bar/15–20°C, waste-heat route and batch injection. Do not transfer its energy/GHG numbers or certify Korean conditions.

issues.finding: Three ships and 20 hhandling do not establish continuous direct well delivery.
issues.action: Keep conditional 62.42% coverage bound for 724 km and 20 h direct windows. Different native injection duration/control/buffering may change it; no five-ship actual design claimed.

issues.finding: Native pipeline hydraulics, standard schedules and 64 candidate optimization unavailable.
issues.action: Retain constant-property/synthetic geometry checks separately. Flange MAOP and material equations are not complete code compliance or reservoir service.

issues.finding: Compression no-scale claim depends on per-train flow/count assumptions.
issues.action: Fixed-count Eq 2 sublinear terms differ from fixed-flow train multiplication. Need native powers and 40 MW allocation; do not infer a full energy balance.

issues.finding: Cost vintages, ton basis and commercial cost/installation inputs unverified.
issues.action: Keep 2015 internet quotes, older correlations, 4%/5% O&M and prices in source context. No current transferable financial benchmark or GHG factor.

issues.finding: Financial 1.6/1.7 liquefaction multipliers do not give actual process duties.
issues.action: No complete capture heat/electricity/compression/liquefaction/cooling/supplier inventory accepted. Preserve missing absolute native outputs.

issues.finding: Hub buffer, handling exclusions and ship-side inventories are unresolved.
issues.action: 2 hparallel-pipe storage is not weather/annual-service assurance. Missing native tank/handling schedule and actual mechanical/phase bounds remain open.

issues.finding: Approximate graphs and twice-cost wording do not reconstruct exact financial arrays.
issues.action: Keep per-tonne/annual-total and component/whole-cost denominators explicit. No guessed half-cost correction or spurious precision from bar heights.

issues.finding: Hub and same-total comparisons change source geography/conditioning.
issues.action: Use matched two-source marginal baselines and appropriate mass weights. Preserve short 60 km/two-route scope rather than a universal hub disadvantage.

issues.finding: Historical deployment and future-capacity recommendations are not verified current operations.
issues.action: Keep plans, policy and overbuilding judgments conditional to demand, time, uncertainty and stranded capacity; no universal technology or climate conclusion.

issues.finding: Only two scoped original edges checked; other originals and all full citation chains remain incomplete.
issues.action: Verify other 43 direct sources, two named authorities and fourteen dependencies; selected passage reading does not complete R013/R035 or their cited models.

issues.finding: Native software, cost/schedule files, SI and licences not supplied or verified.
issues.action: Keep native pipeline, HYSYS, ship optimization, GIS and field models unreproduced. External originals remain paused pending Chrome; no missing-public-asset claim.

issues.finding: Transport-cost evidence does not provide full capture, physical and lifecycle proof for Paper 1.
issues.action: No accepted operating/GHG inputs or numerical results change. Preserve captured/transported/avoided/stored/retained distinctions and existing B2-12 combined 1.5 MPa HOLD.

supplements: No separate SI, code, data or availability statement identified in the retained 21-page article; external availability/version/rights unverified. Article is CC BY 4.0. HYSYS, Clarkson data and prior author models are separate assets and not supplied or licensed by that statement.
reproduction: Thirty-six limited checks, nine steel-conversion rows, four compressor examples, three conditional fleet bounds, seven nominal pure states and four rounded-state corners saved by audit_korea_transport.py. Two selected exact originals checked with narrow scope; their models and full source chains remain open.
paper1_use: Recognize existing conditioning-inclusive transport comparisons and source/geography-dependent mode/hub costs. Qualify the R013 attribution and R035 heating regime. Preserve raw rate/route/state discrepancies and cost boundaries. No B3-07 rows in accepted curated/analysis tables; no source corrections, annual field service, retention or GHG factors accepted. Existing B2-12 combined 1.5 MPa 39.2 HOLD remains unchanged.
